items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: Manuel Perez lived across the street from my grandfather, and he was part of the family.

ctx.x: Well, who did you listen to come?

Well, Manuel Perez lived across the street from my grandfather, and he was part of the family. And there was another old trumpet player that I very seldom hear too much said about, George Moret. And his wife practically helped my mother to bring me up because that's how close-knit all families were here. All of the Creole families down in this area, they're close-knit. And half the time, my mother couldn't find me. I was either at Old Man Jaws Bowl by my grandfather, by Manuel Perez, all over to Bonnie's house,…
Were you any kind of Moret or Parade?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: My grandfather lived right opposite Manuel Perez... I used to watch Manuel when he'd come in from work and when he'd leave.

ctx.x: Yes. You know, if your father might have played with him or something?

Well, sure, we lived around the corner from that. That's how we happened to mention it. That's right. Well, George Moret happens to be, I find this, that over a period of years that these guys giving jazz histories have failed to mention George Moret. He was very conservative and a fellow that wouldn't go out the way to make himself seen or known. But far as playing the cornet, he was one of the best. He was during the time of Manuel, Manuel Perez.
I know Louis Armstrong mentioned him in a series of interviews.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: staying right there with Manuel Perez... you have to learn, otherwise you don't have nothing in your head if you can't learn with these fellas.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. To get back to your very earliest days, we're going to kind of jump around, but... What did you call the neighborhood you lived in? Where you grew up?

The French Quarters. It's all part of the French Quarters. The French Settlement in North Robeson, between Annette and St. Antony. In those days, it was spread out a little more than it is now. Mm-hmm. Go ahead. That's the section there where most of what they said are Creoles were living in. Mm-hmm. And... Bonnie was about a block from me. He was on... he was on Billerish Street. And we all... Manuel Perez was right on Earthquark Street. All of it was concentrated area there.
Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...
